title: Users who logged in this month
statement_markdown: Return each user who logged in during January 2026 at least once. Return unique names sorted alphabetically.

examples.explanation: This output comes from the visible sample data.

hints: Join users to login_events through user_id.
Use a half-open date range: on/after January 1 and before February 1.
explanation: The join connects events to names, the half-open range handles the entire month, and DISTINCT removes repeated logins. A common mistake is including February 1 with BETWEEN. EXISTS is an alternative that naturally avoids duplicate users.
reference_solution: SELECT DISTINCT u.name FROM users u JOIN login_events le ON le.user_id = u.id WHERE le.login_date >= '2026-01-01' AND le.login_date < '2026-02-01' ORDER BY u.name

validation.setup_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id INT, name VARCHAR(50)); CREATE TABLE login_events (id INT, user_id INT, login_date DATE); INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob'), (3, 'Charlie'), (4, 'David'); INSERT INTO login_events VALUES (1, 1, '2026-01-05'), (2, 1, '2026-01-10'), (3, 2, '2026-01-15'), (4, 3, '2025-12-31'), (5, 4, '2026-02-01');
